msg: "manifest_version" is not 3. The Chrome Web Store has only accepted Manifest V3 for new items since 17 January 2022, and Chrome stable no longer runs MV2 extensions. Set "manifest_version": 3 and migrate the MV2-only keys below.
MV2 toolbar key found. "browser_action" and "page_action" do not exist in MV3 - merge both into a single "action" block (same default_popup / default_icon / default_title fields).
The background block is not an MV3 service worker. MV3 accepts only "background": {"service_worker": "sw.js"} (optionally "type": "module") - a background page or a scripts array will not load.
"background.persistent" is an MV2-only key and is invalid in MV3. Delete it; an MV3 service worker is always event-driven and is terminated when idle.
"content_security_policy" is a string. MV3 takes an object: {"extension_pages": "script-src 'self'; object-src 'self'"} and optionally "sandbox".
The CSP allows 'unsafe-eval'. MV3 forbids it in extension_pages; move the evaluated code into a bundled file, or into a "sandbox" page declared in the sandbox CSP.
The CSP allows script from a remote origin. MV3 bans remotely hosted code: every script must ship inside the package, so vendor the library instead of pointing at a CDN.
"web_accessible_resources" is a flat list of paths. MV3 takes objects: [{"resources": ["injected.js"], "matches": ["https://example.com/*"]}] - a flat list fails to load.
A host match pattern is sitting in "permissions". MV3 splits them: API permissions stay in "permissions", every URL pattern moves to "host_permissions".
A host match pattern is sitting in "optional_permissions". In MV3 optional URL patterns belong in "optional_host_permissions".
"webRequestBlocking" is not available to Chrome Web Store items in MV3 (policy-installed enterprise extensions aside). Rewrite the blocking logic as declarativeNetRequest rulesets.
A script is loaded from a URL. The Chrome Web Store rejects remotely hosted code: content scripts and the service worker must reference files bundled in the package.
"update_url" is present. The Chrome Web Store rejects a package that declares its own update URL - keep that key only in a self-hosted build, not in the uploaded ZIP.
"version" is missing or malformed. The store accepts one to four dot-separated integers, each 0-65535 with no leading zero and no suffix, so tags like 1.0.0-beta are rejected at upload.
"name" is missing or longer than the 75-character manifest limit, which stops the upload.
"short_name" is longer than 12 characters. Shorten it, or drop the key and let Chrome truncate "name".
"description" is missing or longer than the 132-character manifest limit. The store listing needs it and refuses a longer one.
No 128x128 icon in "icons". The Chrome Web Store uses the 128px icon for the listing and the install dialog and will not publish without it.
The manifest uses __MSG_ placeholders but sets no "default_locale". Chrome refuses to load a localised manifest without it - add "default_locale" and the matching _locales/<locale>/messages.json.
A "content_scripts" entry has no "matches". Every static content script must declare at least one match pattern or the manifest fails to load.
A "declarative_net_request.rule_resources" entry is missing "id", "enabled" or "path". All three are required and the ruleset is otherwise ignored at load.

Broad host access (<all_urls> or *://*/*) is requested. It is allowed, but it moves the item into extended review and needs a written justification in the dashboard - narrow the pattern if the feature does not need every site.
The "key" field is in the manifest. It is only needed to pin an extension ID during local development - remove it from the uploaded package so the store-assigned ID is used.
"default_locale" is set but neither "name" nor "description" uses a __MSG_ placeholder. Confirm _locales/<locale>/messages.json really exists, or the load fails.
"externally_connectable.matches" contains a wildcard host. Chrome rejects patterns without a fixed domain (and wildcard TLDs) here - name the sites that may message the extension.
